s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral nasal obstruction, facial pain, and diplopia with abducens nerve palsy
salient_findings: Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
key_facts: Woman in her 50s
Presented with bilateral nasal obstruction
Thick nasal discharge
Facial pain and pressure
Condition recalcitrant to 3 prior surgeries, immunotherapy, and medical therapy
Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
Left eye was not proptotic, ecchymotic, or tense
Bedside intraocular pressure measurements: 15 OD, 16 OS (normal)
National Institutes of Health stroke score of 1
Workup results were negative for a cerebrovascular accident

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with painful ophthalmoplegia, including diplopia and abducens nerve palsy, matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause bilateral nasal obstruction, facial pain, and diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement, consistent with the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Gradenigo syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by a triad of symptoms including pain in the distribution of the fifth cranial nerve, abducens nerve palsy, and otitis media, partially matching the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause chronic nasal obstruction, facial pain, and potentially cranial nerve involvement, including diplopia, fitting the patient's long-standing symptoms

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause severe headache, facial pain, and cranial nerve palsies, including abducens nerve palsy, consistent with the patient's presentation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, facial pain and pressure, and the development of binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze and inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline are consistent with Tolosa-Hunt syndrome, which is characterized by painful ophthalmoplegia due to inflammation of the cavernous sinus or superior orbital fissure. The negative workup for cerebrovascular accident and normal intraocular pressure measurements also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient's normal intraocular pressure measurements and lack of proptosis, ecchymosis, or tenseness of the left eye make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Gradenigo syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with a triad of symptoms including otitis media, deep facial pain, and abducens nerve palsy, which does not match the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The patient's condition was recalcitrant to multiple treatments, but there is no mention of fungal infection or other characteristic findings of this condition.

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus abscess
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and negative workup results do not specifically suggest an abscess in the sphenoid sinus.

gold: Transient left abducens (cranial nerve VI) nerve palsy
